title: A generic curve model with finite comparison boundary
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be
projective, with $S$ integral
of finite type over a field, and with geometric fibres of dimension
at most one. After restricting $S$ to a nonempty open, there is a
finite surjection $p:S'\to S$ with $S'$ integral, and a finite
surjection

$$
\nu:Y\longrightarrow T=(X\times_S S')_{\mathrm{red}},
$$

where $Y$ is a finite disjoint union of
smooth projective families of
pure relative dimension one and finite etale families.
Moreover $\nu$ is an isomorphism outside a closed
$D\subset T$ finite over $S'$.

proof.text: For the adapter exists_finite_generic_curve_model, extract the finite-coordinate closed projective embedding from IsHProjective.exists_isClosedImmersion. Factor every field-valued point through its residue field. The finite-type fibre has the same dimension after any field extension, by topologicalKrullDim_pullback_eq_of_field (recorded among the existing source declarations of [lem-pc-dim-base-change]); apply this once to the chosen algebraic closure and once to the given field. This verifies the all-geometric-points hypothesis of the source formulation.

Apply the pre-existing source declaration exists_isFinite_sigmaDesc_genericCurveModel, attached to this same node in lean.declarations. Its remaining sorry is the construction obligation described by the original eleven steps below. It gives a reduced surjective closed immersion T into the iterated pullback, a finite-indexed coproduct comparison and a finite closed boundary. No new existence statement is introduced.

Paste the open-restriction pullback square to identify the iterated pullback with X times_S S′. Compose T into this pullback and factor through its nilradical subscheme using liftNilradical. The lift is a closed immersion by cancellation against the reduction immersion, and it is surjective by surjectivity of the original map and injectivity of the reduction immersion. A surjective closed immersion into a reduced scheme is an isomorphism. Its composite with the reduction inclusion and the base projection is exactly the original structural map.

Reindex the finite family by Fin of its cardinality with Sigma.reindex. Compose the comparison and boundary maps with the reduction isomorphism. Set each structural map equal to the corresponding coprojection followed by the original comparison and structural map. Sigma.hom_ext gives the required over-base equality; each supplied closed embedding gives IsHProjective and hence IsProjective. The complement of the transported boundary is the inverse image of the old complement under the inverse isomorphism. The morphism-restriction composition formula expresses the restricted new comparison as three isomorphisms, so its pullback projection is an isomorphism. The empty coproduct is included.

For the remaining source declaration exists_isFinite_sigmaDesc_genericCurveModel: First replace $S$ by a nonempty affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A$; its generic point remains in this open, and $A$ is a domain. Schemes of finite type over the given field are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Thus all schemes of finite type used below are Noetherian. On their affine charts finite type implies finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation]; separatedness gives quasi-separatedness, so the projective schemes and their finite covers are of finite presentation over their respective ground fields (the original field, $K$, or $\bar K$). A field is Noetherian because its only ideals are zero and the whole field. Put $K=\operatorname{Frac}A$ and choose an algebraic closure $\bar K$. Projectivity survives both the generic-fibre and field base changes by [lem-pc-projective-base-change]. Put $\bar T=(X_{\bar K})_{\mathrm{red}}$; its closed immersion into $X_{\bar K}$ followed by the fixed projective embedding is still a closed immersion (affine-locally it is the composite of surjective quotient maps), so $\bar T$ is projective. Reduction has the same underlying space, hence $\dim\bar T\leq1$.

For the remaining source declaration exists_isFinite_sigmaDesc_genericCurveModel: By [lem-sc-component-intersections-finite], $\bar T$ has finitely many irreducible components. Give each component its reduced closed structure. Normalize each one-dimensional component $C_a$ in its own function field. The identity extension of that field is finite, so [lem-fin-normalization-extension-finite] gives a finite normalization; [lem-sc-normalization-exists] gives surjectivity, birationality and preservation of dimension. Since $\bar K$ is perfect, [lem-sc-normalized-curve-smooth] makes the normalized curves smooth. Each zero-dimensional component is $\operatorname{Spec}\bar K$ by [lem-weil-pbc-zero-dim-integral-point], and is retained unchanged. Take their finite coproduct using [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. The resulting $\bar\nu:\bar Y\to\bar T$ is finite: on an affine chart it corresponds to a finite product of finite modules, with the component inclusions given by quotient maps. It is surjective because the components cover $\bar T$ and each normalization is surjective. Each factor is projective over the affine Noetherian base $\operatorname{Spec}\bar K$ by [lem-fin-finite-over-projective], applied to its finite map to $\bar T$. A smooth integral curve has pure dimension one: the fibre-dimension function is locally constant by [sbc-lem-smooth-relative-dimension-locally-constant], hence constant on the irreducible normalization, and its value is one since its dimension is one. The point factors have relative dimension zero.

For the remaining source declaration exists_isFinite_sigmaDesc_genericCurveModel: The map $\mathcal O_{\bar T}\to\bar\nu_*\mathcal O_{\bar Y}$ is injective. Indeed on an affine chart a section in its kernel vanishes in the function field of every component meeting the chart, by the inclusions into the normalization algebras. It therefore belongs to every minimal prime, hence to every prime, and is nilpotent by [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq]; reducedness makes it zero. The pushforward is coherent by [lem-pc-f3-finite-pushforward-finite-type] and [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth], and its cokernel is coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth]. Its support $\bar E$ is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-module-support-closed]. At each generic point only its own component remains (the other finitely many closed components can be excluded); the normalization induces the same function field by birationality, so the cokernel stalk is zero there. The complement of $\bar E$ is dense. The projective $\bar T$ is separated, of finite type over $\bar K$, and of dimension at most one, hence is a curve in [def-sc-curves], including when it is empty or has isolated point components; [lem-sc-dense-open-finite-complement] makes $\bar E$ a finite set of closed points. Off $\bar E$ the algebra map is an isomorphism and hence $\bar\nu$ is an isomorphism. Thus the generic comparison boundary has dimension at most zero.

proof.text: For the remaining source declaration exists_isFinite_sigmaDesc_genericCurveModel: The finite intermediate extensions $L/K$ in $\bar K$ form a small directed set, with union $\bar K$; their spectra have affine transition maps and are Noetherian and quasi-separated. This is an actual limit diagram: on coordinate rings its colimit is the union $\bar K$. Apply all three clauses of [thm-pd-spreading-out] to $\bar T$, the finitely many factors of $\bar Y$, their maps to $\bar T$, and $\bar T\to X_{\bar K}$, with the existing $X_K$ as the fixed model. Choosing a common finite stage descends the objects, arrows and their commuting relations to a finite extension $K'/K$. The descended $T'\to X_{K'}$ is a closed immersion by [lem-pc-fpqc-descend-closed-immersion], since its pullback to $\bar K$ is one; the covering is fpqc because a field extension is faithfully flat and its spectrum map is affine. Form $Y'$ as the coproduct of the descended factors. Its map $Y'\to T'$ is finite by [lem-sbc-finite-morphism-fpqc-descent], applied to $T'_{\bar K}\to T'$. All these source and target schemes are of finite presentation, as required for the limit theorem.

For the remaining source declaration exists_isFinite_sigmaDesc_genericCurveModel: Identify the descended closed subscheme with the reduction, rather than assuming reduction commutes with field extension. On a chart $\operatorname{Spec}B\subset X_{K'}$, let $I\subset B$ define $T'$. Its extended ideal in $B\otimes_{K'}\bar K$ is the nilradical. Every $b\in I$ therefore has $(b\otimes1)^N=0$ for some $N$, and injectivity of $B\to B\otimes_{K'}\bar K$ implies $b^N=0$. Conversely $B/I$ injects into $(B/I)\otimes_{K'}\bar K$, which is reduced, so $B/I$ is reduced. These two observations give $I=\sqrt{0}$, and glue to $T'=(X_{K'})_{\mathrm{red}}$. Tensor injectivity here is elementary linear algebra: extend a nonzero vector to a field-vector-space basis. No assertion about transcendental extensions is needed. In particular the erroneous exponent $\max N_j$ in the imported proof is not used; if generators satisfy $b_j^{N_j}=0$, a valid exponent for their ideal is $1+\sum_j(N_j-1)$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, identification of the nilradical; elementary faithful field-extension argument

proof.text: For the remaining source declaration exists_isFinite_sigmaDesc_genericCurveModel: Apply [lem-sbc-affine-limit-smooth-stage] to the total descended $Y'$ over the directed system of finite intermediate fields extending $K'$: its pullback to $\bar K$ is smooth. This gives a further finite field stage at which $Y'$ is smooth; replace $K'$ by that stage and all objects by their pullbacks. Each open-and-closed factor is smooth as well. The preceding reduction argument still applies after this replacement. For each factor its dimension at every point equals that at a point above it over $\bar K$, by [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-field-extension], applied on finite-type affine charts. Points above exist because a field extension is faithfully flat (for a prime, the residue-field tensor product is nonzero and has a prime). Thus its relative dimension over $K'$ is exactly the one or zero of its geometric model. Also the map $\mathcal O_{T'}\to\nu'_*\mathcal O_{Y'}$ is injective and its cokernel has dimension-zero support: on affine charts tensoring with $\bar K$ is exact, so the kernel tensors to zero, and [lem-weil-pbc-support-pullback-finite-type] identifies the cokernel's pulled-back support with $\bar E$. The dimensions of its affine support charts are unchanged by [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-preserved-field-extension].

source.place: Proof paragraphs 2-3; Stacks 0C0C (lemma-descend-smooth), field-extension dimension and support comparison

proof.text: For the remaining source declaration exists_isFinite_sigmaDesc_genericCurveModel: Choose finitely many generators $\alpha_i$ of the finite extension $K'/K$. Each satisfies a monic polynomial with coefficients in $K$. Invert the product $a\ne0$ of the denominators of all those coefficients in $A$, so the same polynomials show the $\alpha_i$ integral over $A_a$. Then $A'=A_a[\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r]\subset K'$ is a domain, finite over $A_a$: monomials whose individual exponents are less than the respective monic degrees span it. Its fraction field is $K'$. The injective integral inclusion $A_a\hookrightarrow A'$ gives a surjective spectrum map by [pqf-lem-lying-over]. Therefore $p:S'=\operatorname{Spec}A'\to\operatorname{Spec}A_a$ is finite and surjective. Put $T=(X_{S'})_{\mathrm{red}}$. By [lem-pc-projective-base-change] and the reduction closed immersion, $T$ is projective. Its generic fibre is $T'$: localization commutes with reduction, since if $b/s$ is nilpotent, some nonzero localization denominator $t$ has $tb^n=0$, whence $(tb)^n=0$, so $b/s$ is the localization of a nilpotent element. Conversely localizing a nilpotent stays nilpotent.

source.place: Proof paragraph 4; Stacks 00GU (lemma-integral-going-up); explicit monic-polynomial and localization calculations

proof.text: For the remaining source declaration exists_isFinite_sigmaDesc_genericCurveModel: Use [lem-fin-spread-finite-algebra] over the Noetherian domain $A'$ on the finite coherent $\mathcal O_{T'}$-algebra of $Y'\to T'$, including its finite product decomposition. After inverting one nonzero element of $A'$, it gives a finite $\nu:Y\to T$ and a finite decomposition $Y=\coprod_aY_a$ whose generic factors are the prescribed ones. Each $Y_a\to T$ is finite, because a product factor is a finite quotient of the finite algebra. By [lem-fin-finite-over-projective], all $Y_a$ are projective over this affine open of $S'$. Their finite-type morphisms are of finite presentation by the Noetherian affine-ring criterion [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation].

source.place: Proof paragraph 4, spreading the finite algebra and its factors

proof.text: For the remaining source declaration exists_isFinite_sigmaDesc_genericCurveModel: For the total projective $Y$ over the current affine domain base, apply [lem-sbc-affine-limit-smooth-stage] to the system of principal nonempty base opens $\operatorname{Spec}A'_h$ ($h\ne0$), whose limit is $\operatorname{Spec}K'$. Their transitions are affine, their stages are Noetherian and quasi-separated, and $Y$ is of finite presentation. Its generic fibre is smooth by Step 6, so after one further localization $Y$ and all its factors are smooth. On a factor $Y_a$ of generic relative dimension $n_a\in\{0,1\}$, [sbc-lem-smooth-relative-dimension-locally-constant] says the locus where the fibre dimension is not $n_a$ is closed (indeed open and closed). It has empty generic fibre. Projectivity implies properness by [lem-pc-projective-proper], so its image is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-closed-image]; remove these finitely many images. Now every factor is smooth of pure relative dimension $n_a$. For each $n_a=0$ factor apply [lem-fin-projective-generically-finite] to make its structural map finite by a further nonempty base restriction. Smooth relative dimension zero means etale by [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], so these are finite etale families. The $n_a=1$ factors are the required smooth projective families.

source.place: Proof paragraph 5; Stacks 0C0C (lemma-descend-smooth), 02G1 (lemma-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free), explicit zero-dimensional finiteness step

proof.text:
For the remaining source declaration exists_isFinite_sigmaDesc_genericCurveModel: Let $I=\ker(\mathcal O_T	o
u_*\mathcal O_Y)$ and $Q=\operatorname{coker}(\mathcal O_T	o
u_*\mathcal O_Y)$. Finiteness gives a quasi-coherent finite-type pushforward by [lem-pc-f3-finite-pushforward-finite-type]; on the Noetherian $T$ it is coherent by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]. Hence $I,Q$ are coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth], with closed supports by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-module-support-closed]. Generic localization is exact, so $I$ restricts to zero on $T'$ by Step 6. The support comparison [lem-weil-pbc-support-pullback-finite-type] shows its support misses the generic fibre. This support is a closed subscheme of the projective $T$, therefore projective and proper; [lem-pc-projective-proper] and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-closed-image] allow removal of its closed image from $S'$. Then $I=0$, and [pqf-lem-lying-over], applied on every affine chart to the injective finite algebra map, makes $
u$ surjective. Let $D\subset T$ be the reduced closed subscheme on $\operatorname{Supp}Q$. It is projective and its generic fibre has dimension at most zero by Step 6 and support pullback. Apply [lem-fin-projective-generically-finite] to make $D	o S'$ finite. On $T\setminus D$ the kernel and cokernel vanish, so the finite algebra map is bijective. Taking affine spectra gives that $
u$ is an isomorphism there.

source.place: Proof paragraph 6, kernel, surjectivity and finite cokernel boundary

proof.text: For the remaining source declaration exists_isFinite_sigmaDesc_genericCurveModel: Keep the original finite map $p:S'\to\operatorname{Spec}A_a$ before the subsequent restrictions, and let $V\subset S'$ be the intersection of all the finitely many nonempty opens used in Steps 8-10. Every one contains the unique generic point of the integral $S'$. Its complement $Z=S'\setminus V$ has a reduced closed subscheme structure; its map to $S'$ is finite (quotient algebras are cyclic modules), so $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}A_a$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition]. It is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper] and has closed image by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-closed-image]. That image misses the generic point of $\operatorname{Spec}A_a$, because the generic fibre of $p$ is the one-point $\operatorname{Spec}K'$ and its point is in $V$. Remove the image and choose a nonempty principal affine open $U$ inside the remaining open. Its full inverse image $p^{-1}(U)$ lies in $V$ and is affine and integral. The restricted $p$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence] and surjective (each fibre is the same fibre as for the original surjection). The finite comparison and finite boundary remain finite by the same base-change lemma; projectivity remains by [lem-pc-projective-base-change], and smoothness with its specified relative dimension remains by [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence]. Reduction commutes with this open restriction by the localization argument in Step 7. Renaming $U$ and $p^{-1}(U)$ as $S$ and $S'$ gives every clause of the original statement. Empty generic fibre is included: the coproduct may be empty, and Step 10 removes the entire vertical target by the kernel-support argument.
